A D5 typographic consistency defect; no number or conclusion is affected.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §3.2 "B_wide led B by between -0.12 and -0.01 points across the seven levels (-0.124 points at 20 dB, CI -0.510 to +0.240, 28 of 58 seeds)"
new_issues.competence_basis: Journal-Fit Reviewer persona of the round-2 card (D5 writing_and_structure: terminology and notation that shift between sections); scripted per-block count of U+2212 against ASCII minus before a digit over 41_DRAFT_v5.md
new_issues.attribution_evidence: v4 B0127 (34_DRAFT_v4.md) used U+2212 throughout ('−0.12 and −0.01', '−0.124', 'CI −0.499 to +0.238'); the ASCII hyphens enter with the round-4 replace_block on B0127 (apply report op_index 5, roadmap_item_ids REV-R4-2); B0127 is the only block in v5 with an ASCII minus before a digit.

new_issues.description: §2.4 states that 'all bootstrap intervals use 100,000 resamples of the 58 seeds', but Table S9, which §3.2 and the Supplementary list point to and whose intervals §3.2 B0127 now quotes verbatim, is computed with 20,000 resamples (its caption and tools/make_table_s9.py N_BOOT = 20000, default_rng(0)). As a consequence the registered contrast D − B_wide at 20 dB appears with two different seed-level intervals in the paper: +1.642 to +2.543 in §3.2 B0043, §3.5 B0124, Table 2 and Table 3, and +1.639 to +2.539 in Table S9; the §3.2 intervals for B_wide − B, C_wide − C, D − B and C_wide − B_wide are likewise 20,000-resample values under a Methods sentence that promises 100,000. The differences are at the third decimal and no decision or conclusion changes, but the Methods statement is not true of every interval the paper reports and a methodologist recomputing Table S9 from §2.4's description would not reproduce its interval endpoints.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §2.4 "all bootstrap intervals use 100,000 resamples of the 58 seeds"
new_issues.competence_basis: Statistician-engineer in ML evaluation methodology (round-2 panel seat 2; D1 reporting precision sufficient to recompute); read tools/make_table_s9.py, replayed it with --check (0 hard mismatches) and compared the S9 caption with B0028, B0043, B0124, Table 2 and Table 3
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Present in both versions: B0028's '100,000 resamples' sentence is unchanged from v4 (the round-4 insertion into B0028 is the Bonferroni sentence only), the hand-emitted Table S9 of 2026-10-06 (table_s9_sweep_all_arms.pre-script-20261007.md) already stated '20,000 resamples' in its caption, and v4 B0127 already quoted that table's intervals (e.g. B_wide − B 'CI −0.499 to +0.238', D − B 'CI +1.621 to +2.328'); the round-4 patch only moved B0127 to the script-regenerated values and did not create the discrepancy.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-R4-2 asks that §3.2 agree with Table S9 (it does, exactly); it does not ask that Table S9 or §3.2 agree with §2.4's resample count, and REV-R4-3's four statements do not touch the resample sentence.

new_issues.description: The last sentence of §4.1's third paragraph, 'it shows that at that change the training level, not the architecture, decided most of what happened', sets the training condition against the architecture and applies 'most of' to the outcome of the noise change. Read as a statement about the control arm's 8.8-point loss and its 8.0-point recovery on retraining (the measured quantity the paragraph is about, parallel to §3.5 B0123's 'Most of the gap that the branch closed ... is closed by training at the operating level alone') it is licensed by the data; read as a ranking of the two readings of the 2.097-point evaluation-only benefit (mismatch tolerance against weak-component protection) it would contradict the same section's 'the design cannot say which'. The sentence does not name the benefit and was not counted as apportionment under REV-R4-1 test (a), but the ambiguity is the one the panel spent two rounds removing elsewhere and a hostile reader can take it the second way.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §4.1 "It concerns a change of noise level within one instrument model and one reconstructor, and it shows that at that change the training level, not the architecture, decided most of what happened."
new_issues.competence_basis: Statistician-engineer in ML evaluation methodology (round-2 panel seat 2; D3 argumentative_coherence: a claim stated in one section must not contradict the claim stated in another); exhaustive regex scan of §4.1–4.2 for the apportionment vocabulary the committed criterion lists
new_issues.attribution_evidence: B0053 is byte-identical between 34_DRAFT_v4.md and 41_DRAFT_v5.md (apply report: not among the 11 touched blocks; my own block diff confirms), and the same sentence stood in v4 when the round-3 verifier scored REV-R3-1 and named only B0056 and B0051 as residuals.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-R4-1's test (a) is defined on sentences that quantify or rank how much of the evaluation-only 20 dB benefit belongs to each reading; this sentence quantifies the outcome of the noise change as a whole (dominated by the control arm's loss), which the committed record itself classes as a measured quantity rather than a reading in its treatment of B0123, so it is adjacent to the item but not inside its criterion.

A one-phrase completeness gap in the unregistered-analysis disclosure.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §2.6 "the contrast of D against the unwidened arm B at 40 dB (Section 3.1)"

Letter header on Table S9: 'means and lead counts identical' is exact (35 of 35 cells agree on mean and lead count between table_s9_sweep_all_arms.pre-script-20261007.md and the script output); 'intervals differ in the third decimal' understates it — endpoints move by up to 0.013 (B_wide − B at 20 dB: −0.499 → −0.510; C_wide − C: −0.385/+0.445 → −0.387/+0.452; C_wide − B_wide: +0.003/+0.851 → +0.005/+0.862), i.e. at the second decimal. §3.2 cites the script values throughout, so no number in the manuscript is affected, and the conclusion that the earlier RNG seed was unrecorded is the honest account. The 38_ Residual Issue 3 reference values (−0.385 to +0.445), inherited into the Phase-1 operationalization, are the superseded ones; 2A scored the script values under equivalence_policy, so the letter's 'superseded' note changes nothing.

REV-R4-2 / NEW-1: the letter writes every negative number in its REV-R4-2 row with U+2212 ('CI −0.387 to +0.452'), whereas the manuscript sentence it describes (B0127 line 158; 43_ line 120) uses ASCII hyphen-minus for the same five numbers. The letter is typographically right and the text is not; the authors evidently did not notice the glyph change the patch introduced. NEW-1 stands as frozen.

NEW-1 scope note for the patch: the ASCII hyphen-minus is confined to B0127 in 41_ (v4 had none; v5 has five, all on line 158), but the rendered deliverable 43_SUBMISSION_scirep_v5.md also writes negatives with ASCII hyphens inside its table rows (lines 330–377: Tables 1–3 and the retrained-contrast table, 44 further instances) because the results/tables/*.md sources do. Restoring U+2212 in B0127 makes the prose consistent with the rest of the prose, as NEW-1 asks; the table glyphs are a separate rendering convention of the table files and were not raised by 2A, so they are noted here and not scored.

NEW-2: the letter's own header documents the discrepancy NEW-2 names without noticing it — it states that the S9 intervals come from tools/make_table_s9.py (20,000 resamples, default_rng(0)) and that 'the script's values are the ones cited in §3.2', while §2.4 B0028 (untouched by this round's insertion) still promises 'all bootstrap intervals use 100,000 resamples of the 58 seeds'. Closing NEW-2 is a one-clause Methods edit (exempt Table S9 and the §3.2 width contrasts from the 100,000 statement, or regenerate S9 at 100,000 resamples) — decision-inert, previously_missed.

NEW-3: the letter does not mention B0053 ('the training level, not the architecture, decided most of what happened'); B0053 is byte-identical to v4 and the authors' REV-R4-1 row treats the two named blocks as the whole of the residual. The ambiguity 2A recorded remains open and is decision-inert.
